cues.en: And so on and so on up the stack, ensuring that you know which programs are running on your computer and that any programs running in secret have gotten there by leveraging a defect in the bootloader or the operating system or the other components and not because this computer was designed to actually hide things from you. Now this story always reminds me of Descartes. You know, he starts off by saying that he can't tell what's true and what's not true because he doesn't know if he can trust his senses, doesn't know if he can trust his reason. So he does some mental gymnastics which I won't get into here, although that's generally the thing people find interesting about him. But what's interesting to me is that once he establishes this tiny little nub of certainty,
cues.zh: 如此沿着技术栈层层向上，确保你能清楚计算机上运行着哪些程序；任何暗中运行的程序，都只能是通过利用 bootloader、操作系统或其他组件的缺陷溜进来的，而不是因为这台电脑被设计出来故意瞒着你。这总让我想起笛卡尔。你知道，他一开始说自己分不清真伪，因为他不知道能否相信自己的感官，不知道能否相信自己的理性。于是他进行了一番思想体操——这里我就不细说了，尽管大家通常觉得那才是他最有趣的地方。但我觉得有意思的是，一旦他确立了这一点点微小的确定性之核，

cues.en: a kind of mental gymnastic exercise that says, Oh, I can trust my reason. I can trust my senses. Then he is able to erect this kind of stable
cues.zh: 一种告诉自己“我可以相信理性、可以相信感官”的思想体操，接着他就能够建立起某种稳固的

cues.en: edifice
cues.zh: 大厦，

cues.en: of a worldview on it. Right? He knows one thing to be true and everything else can be hung off of that one thing. He can build it up. Now a TPM is like that. It's a nub of stable certainty. If it's there, it can reliably inform you about your bootloader and then... And thus your operating system and thus the process is running on your computer. Now you may find it weird to hear someone like me talking warmly about TPMs.
cues.zh: 一座世界观的大厦。对吧？他知道一件事是确凿的，其他一切都可以挂靠在这个支点之上，层层构建。TPM 也是如此，它是一个稳固的确定性之核。只要它在，就能可靠地告诉你 bootloader 的状态，进而……进而确认你的操作系统，再进而确认电脑上运行的进程。听到像我这样的人对 TPM 赞不绝口，你可能会觉得奇怪。

cues.en: After all, these are the technologies that make it possible to lock phones,
cues.zh: 毕竟，正是这类技术让锁定手机成为可能，

cues.en: tablets,
cues.zh: 还有平板电脑、

cues.en: consoles, even some PCs, so that they won't run software of the owner's choosing.
cues.zh: 游戏主机，甚至某些 PC 也不例外，导致它们无法运行设备所有者自行挑选的软件。

cues.en: Jailbreaking usually means finding a way to subvert a TPM.
cues.zh: 越狱通常就意味着要想方设法绕过 TPM。

cues.en: Why on earth would I want a TPM in my computer? Well, as with everything interesting in tech and policy, the devil is in the details.
cues.zh: 那我到底为什么会想要电脑里有个 TPM 呢？正如科技与政策领域所有有趣的事情一样，魔鬼藏在细节中。

cues.en: Now imagine for a moment that there's two different ways of implementing a TPM. There may be more, but imagine these two.
cues.zh: 现在设想一下，TPM 有两种不同的实现方式。可能还有更多，但姑且想象这两种。

cues.en: The first one we'll call lockdown.
cues.zh: 第一种我们称之为“封锁”模式。

cues.en: So in the lockdown world, your TPM comes with a set of signing keys that it trusts, and unless your bootloader appears in that list of signing... Is signed by one of those signing keys,
cues.zh: 在封锁模式的世界里，TPM 自带一组它信任的签名密钥，除非你的 bootloader 出现在签名列表……由其中一个签名密钥签名，

cues.en: it won't run it. It won't boot. The operating system won't run. You're just... You're stuck there in whatever it is the people who installed
cues.zh: 否则它就不会运行。系统无法引导，操作系统也跑不起来。你就……被困死在那里，只能运行那些

cues.en: the bootloader on your computer
cues.zh: 在你电脑上安装 bootloader 的人

cues.en: want you to run, and you can't change that. Now there's another mode that I'll call certainty.
cues.zh: 想让你运行的东西，而且你无力改变。现在还有另一种模式，我称之为“确定性”模式。

cues.en: And in the certainty mode, you tell your TPM which signing keys you trust. The first time you turn your computer on, you initialize it with some authentication token, whoops, like a key or a password
cues.zh: 在确定性模式下，由你来告诉 TPM 你信任哪些签名密钥。首次开机时，你用某种认证凭据（哎呀，比如密钥或密码）初始化它，

cues.en: or
cues.zh: 或者

cues.en: some other thing, a biometric that it knows, so it knows who it belongs to. And then you, the owner, are the only person who gets to say what it trusts. And so you can say, I don't trust this person's operating system or I do trust that person's operating system. Only run operating systems that are signed by Canonical, EFF, ACLU, or WikiLeaks.
cues.zh: 某种其他凭据，比如它能识别的生物特征，这样它就知道自己属于谁了。然后，作为所有者的你，就是唯一有权决定它信任什么的人。这样你就可以说：我不信任这个人的操作系统，或者我信任那个人的操作系统；只运行由 Canonical、EFF、ACLU 或 WikiLeaks 签名的操作系统。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: approximately speaking,
cues.zh: 粗略地说，

cues.en: these two modes correspond to, of course, iOS and Android.
cues.zh: 这两种模式自然对应的就是 iOS 和 Android。

cues.en: And iOS only lets you run the code that's been approved by Apple. Android lets you tick a box and say, I'm a grown up. Let me choose who I trust. But critically, Android lacks an important facility. It lacks the facility to verify
cues.zh: iOS 只允许你运行经过 Apple 审核的代码。Android 则允许你勾选一个选项，表示“我是成年人了，让我自己选信任谁”。但关键在于，Android 缺少一个重要机制：它无法验证

cues.en: that what you think you're running is what you are running. It's freedom without certainty.
cues.zh: “你以为你在跑的程序，到底是不是真正跑的程序”。这是一种缺乏确定性的自由。

cues.en: Now freedom without certainty is a big deal in a world where the computers were just... Were discussing can see you and hear you, where you put them in your pocket and take them into the toilet, where they sit by your bedside, where they fly airplanes, where we put our bodies into them and they drive our cars around. Which is why I like the idea of a TPM,
cues.zh: 而缺乏确定性的自由是个大问题，尤其在当下——我们刚刚讨论的电脑能看到你、听到你，你把它们揣在兜里带进厕所，它们立在你的床头，它们开着飞机，甚至我们坐进车里，由它们接管驾驶。这就是为什么我很赞成 TPM 这个理念，

cues.en: provided it's implemented in the certainty mode and not in the lockdown mode.
cues.zh: 前提是它以“确定性模式”实现，而非“锁定模式”。

cues.en: Now if that's not clear, think of it this way. There's the war on general purpose computation and that's what happens when control freaks and governments or companies decide that they should have the final say in what you do on your computer.
cues.zh: 如果这还不够清晰，可以这样理解：存在一场针对通用计算的战争，那是当政府或公司的控制狂们认定，他们必须对你在电脑上做什么拥有最终决定权时发生的事。

cues.en: There's also
cues.zh: 另外，

cues.en: and then there's this. There's the counter position, which is that defenders against those people are also control freaks, but they're control freaks like me. We want to be the people with the ultimate destiny
cues.zh: 还有这样一种对立立场：反抗那些人的人其实也是控制狂，只是他们是像我这样的控制狂。我们希望掌控最终命运，

cues.en: over what we install on our computers. Both sides want control, they just differ in where the nexus of control should be. And control requires knowledge. If you want to be sure that the songs that are moved onto an iPod stay on the iPod and
cues.zh: 决定在自己的电脑上安装什么。双方都想要控制权，分歧只在于控制的核心归谁。而控制需要知情。如果你想确保导入 iPod 的歌曲只能留在 iPod 上，

cues.en: not... And don't come off of the iPod, the iPod needs to know
cues.zh: 绝不能被导出来，iPod 就必须知道，

cues.en: that the instructions that it's getting are coming from an Apple approved version of iTunes and not one pretending to be iTunes. Otherwise, you don't get the Roach Motel.
cues.zh: 它接收的指令来自 Apple 认证的 iTunes，而不是冒牌的 iTunes。否则，你的“蟑螂屋”就建不成了。

cues.en: If you want to be sure that my PVR
cues.zh: 如果你想确保我的 PVR

cues.en: won't record a watch once video on demand program, or if it does record a program that it won't output it to anything except something that will, honor whatever business rules came along with it. You have to be sure that you know what programs I'm running and what they do.
cues.zh: 不会录制“仅限观看一次”的点播视频；或者即便录了，也绝不会输出给任何不遵守附带商业规则的设备。你就必须确保自己知道我运行了什么程序，以及它们都在做什么。

cues.en: But if I wanna be sure that you aren't watching me through my webcam,
cues.zh: 但如果我想确保你没有通过摄像头偷窥我，

cues.en: I need to know what firmware is running, and I need to know that the little green light always comes on when my webcam switches itself on. If I don't wanna be sure that you aren't capturing my passwords through my keyboard using a software keylogger,
cues.zh: 我就需要知道上面跑的是什么固件，需要确信只要摄像头一启动，小绿灯就一定会亮。如果我想确保你没有通过键盘记录软件截获我的密码，

cues.en: I need to know that the OS isn't lying when it says there aren't any keyloggers resident in the system. Whether you want to be free or whether you want to enslave, you need control and you need knowledge.
cues.zh: 我就必须知道操作系统在声称系统内没有常驻键盘记录器时，并没有撒谎。无论你是想获得自由还是想奴役他人，你都需要控制权，也都需要知情权。

cues.en: So that's the coming war on general purpose computation.
cues.zh: 那么，这就是即将到来的通用计算之战。

cues.en: And now I want to investigate what happens if we win it. And that's the civil war over general purpose computation.
cues.zh: 现在我想研究一下，如果我们赢了会发生什么。那就是围绕通用计算的内部战争。

cues.en: So now let's stipulate that there that we have a victory for the freedom side and it means that we have computers where owners always know what's running on them because the computers would faithfully report the hash and the associated signatures for any bootloaders they find and control over what was running on the computers goes to you because the computers would allow their owners to specify who was allowed to sign their bootloaders'
cues.zh: 那么现在我们姑且假定，自由阵营取得了胜利，这意味着我们拥有的计算机，其所有者总能知道上面在运行什么，因为计算机会忠实报告它们发现的任何引导加载程序的哈希值和相关签名；对计算机上运行内容的控制权也归你，因为计算机会允许其所有者指定谁有权签署他们的引导加载程序、

cues.en: operating systems and so on. Now there are two arguments you can make in favor of this victory, why this victory would be a good one. The first one is a human rights argument. If your world is made of computers, then designing computers to override their owners' decisions has significant
cues.zh: 操作系统等等。现在，你可以提出两个支持这场胜利的论点，说明为什么这场胜利会是好事。第一个是人权论点。如果你的世界由计算机组成，那么设计计算机去推翻其所有者的决定，会带来重大的

cues.en: human rights implications.
cues.zh: 人权影响。

cues.en: And today there are people who worry that the Iranian government might demand import controls so that all the computers that come in have a UEFI style boot locker that only boots
cues.zh: 而今天有人担心，伊朗政府可能要求进口管制，让所有进口的计算机都带有一个 UEFI 式启动锁，只能启动

cues.en: operating systems that have lawful interception backdoors built in. So you can move the spying right to the edge, the user of the computer, the owner of the computer. But tomorrow it may be that, I live in The UK and it may be that our home secretary says if the NHS gives you a cochlear implant, it has to intercept and report all the extremist speech it hears.
cues.zh: 内置合法拦截后门的操作系统。这样就能把监视直接推到边缘，也就是计算机用户、计算机所有者。但明天可能会变成，我住在英国，可能我们的内政大臣会说，如果 NHS 给你植入人工耳蜗，它必须拦截并报告它听到的所有极端主义言论。

cues.en: So the human rights stuff is easy to understand. The second argument comes from property rights. Now the doctrine of first sale is a very important piece of law. It says once you buy something, you own it. You should have the freedom to do anything you want to it even if it gores the ox of the person who sold it to you. DRM opponents like me, we love the slogan, You bought it, you own it.
cues.zh: 所以人权那一套很容易理解。第二个论点来自产权。首次销售原则是一条非常重要的法律。它说，一旦你买了某样东西，你就拥有它。你应当有自由对它做任何你想做的事，哪怕这触怒了卖给你的人。像我这样的 DRM 反对者，很喜欢这句口号：你买了，你就拥有它。

cues.en: Now property rights are an incredibly powerful argument to have on your side anywhere,
cues.zh: 产权作为己方论据，在任何场合都极其强大，

cues.en: but they're especially powerful to have on your side in a nerdfight
cues.zh: 但在一场极客论战中，站在你这边的产权尤其强大

cues.en: because you can't swing a cat in Silicon Valley without hitting someone who thinks that property rights are an important way of solving most social problems.
cues.zh: 因为在硅谷，你随便碰上个人，都是认为产权是解决大多数社会问题的重要方式的人。

cues.en: But it's not just nerdfights.
cues.zh: 但这不只是极客论战。

cues.en: Copy fighters get really pissed off about the term intellectual property because property is also a really good way to win arguments in policy circles. Before the term intellectual property came into prominence we had other terms like creator's monopoly.
cues.zh: 版权斗士对“知识产权”这个说法非常恼火，因为“财产”也是在政策圈赢得争论的绝佳方式。在“知识产权”一词流行起来之前，我们还有别的说法，比如“创作者垄断”。

cues.en: And it's very hard to go to a regulator or a lawmaker and say, My monopoly isn't large enough. But going and saying, My property rights are being not
cues.zh: 而且你很难去找监管者或立法者说：“我的垄断还不够大。” 但你去说：“我的产权没有得到

cues.en: respected enough or need to be expanded so that I can make sure that they're policed adequately,
cues.zh: 足够尊重，或者需要扩展，好让我能确保它们得到充分执法，

cues.en: that's a very powerful argument to have on your hand.
cues.zh: 那就会是你手里非常有力的论点。

cues.en: That's where the Civil War part comes in. Human rights and property rights both demand that computers not be designed for remote control
cues.zh: 这就是“内战”爆发的根源。人权和财产权都要求，计算机绝不能被设计成

cues.en: by
cues.zh: 任由

cues.en: corporations or governments.
cues.zh: 大公司或政府远程控制。

cues.en: Owners should be allowed to specify their OS and the programs running on them to freely choose that nub of certainty in the void that allows them to build their whole
cues.zh: 所有者应当有权指定操作系统及运行的程序，自由选择虚空中的那个确定性支点，从而在此之上构建起

cues.en: stable edifice of certainty on. Now remember that security is relative. You are secured from attacks on your ability to freely use your music
cues.zh: 稳固的确定性大厦。请记住，安全性是相对的。你可以免受他人剥夺你自由使用音乐

cues.en: environment. But if you can control your computing environment,
cues.zh: 环境的攻击。但如果你能控制自己的计算环境，

cues.en: the Recording Industry Association of America is now vulnerable to attacks on their ability to rent you music on a single use basis.
cues.zh: 美国唱片业协会就会陷入被动，无法再按“单次使用”向你出租音乐。

cues.en: We have this notion of streaming, this consensus hallucination that there's a difference between a stream and a download as though there's some means of transmitting a stream of bits to someone's computer without actually having them download that stream of bits like the Internet is made of mirrors and speaking tubes. We
cues.zh: 我们有了“流媒体”的概念，产生了一种群体幻觉，以为“流传输”和“下载”有什么本质不同，仿佛有某种方法能把比特流传输到某人的电脑上，却不需要对方实际下载一样，就好像互联网全是由镜子和传声管构成的。我们

cues.en: say stream, we mean I think that your
cues.zh: 所谓的流媒体，意思其实就是

cues.en: receiving software doesn't have a Save As button.
cues.zh: 你的接收软件上没有“另存为”按钮。

cues.en: Now if you get to choose the nub from which the scaffold dangles,
cues.zh: 如果你能决定悬挂脚手架的支点，

cues.en: you get control and power to secure yourself against people who attack your interests.
cues.zh: 你就拥有了控制权和力量，保护自己不受侵害自身利益之人的攻击。

cues.en: Now if the Recording Industry Association of America or the government or Monsanto get to choose the nub, they get control and the power to secure themselves against you.
cues.zh: 但如果由美国唱片业协会、政府或孟山都来决定这个支点，他们就掌握了控制权，有能力防范你。

cues.en: So we all agree that at the very least owners should control what runs on their computer, or at least I'll ask you to stipulate that. Now what about users of computers?
cues.zh: 所以我们都认同，所有者至少应该能控制自己电脑上运行什么，或者至少我希望大家先承认这点。但计算机的使用者呢？

cues.en: Users of computers don't always have the same interests as owners of computers.
cues.zh: 计算机的使用者和所有者的利益并不总是一致。

cues.en: Increasingly,
cues.zh: 越来越普遍的是，

cues.en: we will all be users of computers that we don't own.
cues.zh: 我们使用的都是自己并不拥有的计算机。

cues.en: Where you come down on the conflict between owners and users of computers,
cues.zh: 在所有者与使用者的冲突中你作何选择，

cues.en: I think is going to end up being one of the most important both technological and moral questions of the coming decades.
cues.zh: 我认为这最终会成为未来数十年内最重要的技术兼道德议题之一。

cues.en: And there's no easy answer I have, no bright line for when users or owners should trump one another when it comes to computers.
cues.zh: 对此我也没有现成的简单答案，在计算机问题上，使用者和所有者究竟谁的权益该压过谁，并没有清晰的分界线。

cues.en: Now let's start with the position I'll call property maximalism.
cues.zh: 现在我们先来看看我称之为“产权至上主义”的立场。

cues.en: If I own my computer, I should have the absolute right to dictate terms
cues.zh: 如果电脑是我的，我就应该有绝对的权利向任何想使用它的人

cues.en: to anyone who wants to use it. If you don't like it, find someone else's computer to use. This one's mine. I set the rules. How would that work in practice? Well,
cues.zh: 提条件。不接受，就去找别人的电脑用。这台是我的，我说了算。那实际该怎么实现？

cues.en: you got some combination of an initialization routine where you set the root of trust, tamper evidence, law, and physical control. For example, you turn your computer on for the first time and you initialize a good secret password possibly signed by your private key, And without that key, no one is allowed to change the list of trusted parties who's are allowed to sign your bootloader.
cues.zh: 你需要结合初始化流程来设置信任根、防篡改机制、法律以及物理控制。例如，首次开机时设置一个私密密码，并可能用私钥进行签名，如果没有这把密钥，任何人都不能更改有权对 bootloader 签名的受信任方列表。

cues.en: And we can make it against the law to subvert this for the purpose of taking control away from the owner. That makes
cues.zh: 我们还可以立法规定，为夺走所有者控制权而颠覆这套机制是违法的。这会让

cues.en: writing malware that hijacks your computer extra special, super duper illegal.
cues.zh: 编写劫持你电脑的恶意软件，变得格外、超级加倍违法。

cues.en: But it also makes
cues.zh: 但这也会让

cues.en: stealthy DRM installation even more illegal.
cues.zh: 隐蔽安装 DRM 更加违法。

cues.en: And we can design the TPMs that if you remove it or tamper with it, it's really obvious. You give it a fragile housing so that when it's changed
cues.zh: 我们还可以把 TPM 设计成：一旦你移除或篡改它，就会非常明显。给它一个易碎外壳，这样当它被换

cues.en: out, you can tell at a glance that it's happened. And then if you still trust physical locks, you can put it under lock and key too. Now I can see a lot of benefits to this, but there are unquestionably some downsides to giving owners absolute control over their computers. And one wedge issue is probably going to be a self driving car. cues.en: For example, you may remember that there was widespread indignation from all sides when it was revealed that employers were asking prospective employees to turn over their Facebook login credentials.
cues.zh: 比如，大家可能还记得，当初有报道曝光某些雇主要求求职者交出 Facebook 登录凭证时，引发了各方普遍的愤怒。

cues.en: Employers argued that they needed to be able to review your list of friends, what you said to them and what you did with them, in order to make sure that you didn't have any skeletons in your closet that compromise your ability to work for them. Facebook logins were fast on their way to becoming the workplace urine test of the twenty first century.
cues.zh: 雇主辩称，他们需要查看你的好友列表、你和他们说了什么、做了什么，以此确保你没有什么见不得人的黑历史会影响工作表现。Facebook 登录凭证一度迅速沦为 21 世纪职场的新型“尿检”。

cues.en: A means of ensuring that your private life didn't have any unsavory secrets lurking in it, secrets that might compromise your work life. Now the country wasn't buying this. From Senate hearings to op eds, the country rose up against this practice.
cues.zh: 成了一种确保你的私生活中没有潜藏任何见不得人的秘密、免得影响工作生活的手段。但公众并不买账。从参议院听证会到各大媒体社论，全美上下都奋起抵制这种做法。

cues.en: But no one seemed to mind
cues.zh: 但似乎没人介意的是，

cues.en: that many employers routinely insert their own intermediate keys into their employees' devices, their phones, their tablets, their computers that allows them to spy on their employees' internet traffic even when it's secure with a little lock showing in their browser.
cues.zh: 许多雇主常规性地在员工的手机、平板和电脑等设备中植入自己的中间密钥，借此窥探员工的网络流量，即便浏览器上显示着代表连接安全的小锁标志也不例外。

cues.en: This gives your employer access to all your sensitive, all the sensitive sites you access while you're on the job from your union's message board to your bank website to your Gmail to your HMO or the private repository managed by your doctor's office to Facebook.
cues.zh: 这让你的雇主能访问你工作期间访问的所有敏感网站，从工会留言板、银行网站、Gmail，到你的医保机构或诊所管理的私人档案库，再到 Facebook。

cues.en: Now there's a wide consensus that this is okay because the laptop, the phone, and the tablet that your employer issues to you are not your property, they're company property.

cues.en: And yet the reason that employers give us these mobile devices is because there's no longer any meaningful distinction between home and work, between personal life and professional life. cues.en: And of course in America we have the land of the fifty five plus hour work week where few professionals take any meaningful vacation time and when they do get away for a day or two they bring their BlackBerry alarm.
cues.zh: 当然，在美国这个每周工作 55 小时以上的国度，几乎没有专业人士能真正休个像样的假，哪怕离开一两天，也得随身带着 BlackBerry。

cues.en: Even in the old pre digital traditional workplace, we recognized that workers had human rights. We didn't put cameras in the toilets to curtail employee theft.
cues.zh: 哪怕是在过去前数字化时代的老式职场中，我们也承认劳动者是有基本人权的。我们不会为了防范员工偷窃而在洗手间里装摄像头。

cues.en: Now before I discussed how an owner override might work. You'd have some combination of physical access control and tamper evidence designed to give owners of computers the power to know and control what bootloader and OS was running on their machine.
cues.zh: 此前我讨论过所有者覆盖可能如何运作。你会用物理访问控制和篡改证据的某种组合，让计算机所有者能够知道并控制自己的机器上运行的是什么 bootloader 和操作系统。

cues.zh: 那么用户覆盖将如何运作？

cues.en: so that when the owner takes it back, can be sure that it's in the state that she believed it was in when she handed it over. In other words, we need to protect users from owners and owners from users as well as users from other users.

cues.en: Now here's one model for that and this is the hypothetical. I'm not suggesting we do this, I'm suggesting it by way of example.
cues.zh: 这里有一个模型，这是假设性的。我不是建议我们这样做，只是举例说明。

cues.en: Imagine that there's a bootloader that can reliably and accurately report on the kernels and OSs it finds on your computer.
cues.zh: 想象有一个 bootloader，能可靠而准确地报告它在你的计算机上找到的内核和操作系统。

cues.en: Now this is a prerequisite for all the scenarios we've discussed, the one in which the state controls your computer, the one in which the owner controls your computer, and the one in which users may be able to control their computer some of the time. Now give the bootloader the power to suspend any running operating system to disk, encrypting all its thread and parking them. And the power to select another operating system from the network or an external drive. So I walk into an internet cafe
cues.zh: 这是我们所讨论的所有场景的前提：国家控制你的计算机、所有者控制你的计算机，以及用户有时可能控制自己的计算机。现在赋予 bootloader 这样的能力：把任何正在运行的操作系统挂起到磁盘，加密其所有线程并将它们停放；还能从网络或外部驱动器选择另一个操作系统。于是我走进一家网吧

cues.en: and there's an OS running that I can verify
cues.zh: 那里运行着一个我能验证的操作系统

cues.en: and it has a lawful interception backdoor for the police.
cues.zh: 而且它有一个供警方使用的合法监听后门。

cues.en: It stores all my keystrokes, it stores all my files, all my screens, and an encrypted blob that the state can decrypt.
cues.zh: 它记录我所有的击键，存储我所有的文件、所有屏幕画面，以及一个政府能解密的加密数据块。

cues.en: Now I'm an attorney or a doctor or a corporate executive or just a human being who doesn't want all of his communications
cues.zh: 而我是律师、医生、企业高管，或者只是一个不想让自己所有通信

cues.en: being available to anyone who can bribe a cop.
cues.zh: 被任何能贿赂警察的人获取。

cues.en: So I do some kind of three finger salute on my keyboard and it drops into a minimal bootloader shell and I can give the net address of an alternative operating system or insert a thumb drive. Now the cafe owner's operating system gets parked, I can't see inside it, But the bootloader can assure me that it's dormant and not spying on me as my operating system fires up. And when it's done, all my working files are trashed and the bootloader confirms it, not just because this keeps the computer's owner from spying on me, but it keeps me from spying on the computer's owner.
cues.zh: 于是我在键盘上做出某种三指礼，它进入一个最小化的 bootloader shell，我可以输入另一个操作系统的网络地址，或者插入 U 盘。现在网吧老板的操作系统被挂起，我看不到它内部，但 bootloader 能向我保证它处于休眠状态，并且在我的操作系统启动时没有监视我。等这一切结束后，我所有的工作文件都被销毁，bootloader 会确认这一点；不仅因为这能防止计算机所有者监视我，也防止我监视计算机所有者。
